basis: Leukocyte infection with cytopenias; hepatic inflammation with aminotransferase elevation occurs in roughly 70-90%, supporting common hepatocellular injury.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic inflammation and biochemical hepatocellular injury occur in roughly 70-90%; persistent liver failure is not required.

basis: Metabolic enzyme deficiency with common neurologic dysfunction (>30%); cardiomyopathy reported in 1/2 assessed patients. Cardiac frequency is uncertain because of the small sample.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 1/2 assessed patients supports inclusion under the supplied HPO evidence, with limited precision.
decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental impairment and brain degeneration are common manifestations of the metabolic defect; brain atrophy is reported in 1/2.

basis: Predisposition targets infantile capillary vascular tumors, predominantly arising in skin; no additional organ damage follows from susceptibility alone.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the predisposition specifically targets tumors of capillary blood vessels, which fall within the cardiovascular axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: infantile capillary hemangiomas predominantly arise in skin, making skin a usual target of this defined predisposition.

basis: Mycobacterial infection predominantly located in the lungs; individual extrapulmonary sites do not meet the common-involvement threshold across the umbrella.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: lungs are the predominant anatomical site explicitly described in the definition and characterize the usual disease.

basis: Skeletal abnormalities (5/5-6/6) and dental crowding (4/4); CNS defects/delay in assessed 1/1-2/2 and pulmonary artery stenosis 2/2. Sparse endocrine, renal and airway findings omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: pulmonary artery stenosis in 2/2 assessed patients, with other major cardiac and arterial abnormalities reported; denominators are small.
decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay and structural CNS abnormalities recur in assessed subsets of 1/1-2/2; skeletal and dental findings establish the core phenotype.

basis: Disease of retinal capillaries: the retina establishes ocular location and structural vascular abnormalities establish cardiovascular involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: telangiectasia is a structural disorder of retinal blood vessels; the cardiovascular axis includes capillaries without requiring systemic disease.

basis: Dirofilaria infection commonly occupies subcutaneous tissue, producing persistent parasitic nodules in >30% of human cases; pulmonary and ocular frequencies vary geographically.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: subcutaneous parasitic nodules account for >30% of human cases overall and represent direct tissue occupation and inflammation.

basis: Defining digital/oral malformations and pituitary disease; GH deficiency 6/7. Developmental delay 4/5 with structural brain defects. Ptosis 2/6 omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay affects 4/5, with recurrent structural brain malformations; retained alongside the three defining primary axes.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: pituitary malformations and hormone deficiencies characterize this subtype; GH deficiency occurs in 6/7 and TSH deficiency in 4/7.

basis: Inherited mitochondrial pyrophosphatase deficiency disrupts pyrophosphate metabolism and causes myocardial fibrosis with alcohol-triggered cardiac failure.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this PPA2-related condition is a mitochondrial pyrophosphatase deficiency, an inborn metabolic disorder underlying the cardiac phenotype.

basis: Temple syndrome features motor developmental delay, precocious puberty and obesity. Joint hypermobility (12/19) lacks documented tissue damage; scoliosis occurs in 7/30 (<30%).

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: hypermobility in 12/19 establishes laxity without demonstrated joint damage or functional loss; scoliosis in 7/30 is below threshold.
